_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-08-03 07:50:16Z)**_

This is a Node/Vite application. On your PC, the installed Node version is **20.14.0**, but this project requires **Node 22.13 or newer**.

In PowerShell:

```powershell
cd D:\Dropbox\windowsdesktop\loan-statement-calculator
```

Upgrade Node using the installer from https://nodejs.org/ — choose the current LTS version. Then close and reopen PowerShell and confirm:

```powershell
node --version
```

It should report `v22.13.0` or newer. Then run:

```powershell
cd D:\Dropbox\windowsdesktop\loan-statement-calculator
npm ci
npx vite
```

Open the address printed by Vite, normally:

```text
http://localhost:5173
```

Stop the application with `Ctrl+C`.

Use `npx vite` on Windows rather than `npm run dev`: the repository’s packaged development command uses Linux-style environment-variable syntax and may fail in PowerShell.

One caveat: this application uses a local Cloudflare D1 database. Its first screen should direct you to `/setup`, but the database migrations may need applying if you receive a `no such table: users` error.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-08-03 07:52:57Z)**_

You’re right: for a simple calculator, this is overengineered.

This method was chosen because the project was built from an **OpenAI Sites / Cloudflare starter**, not from a minimal desktop calculator template. It includes infrastructure for:

- Cloudflare Workers and D1 database
- User login and password management
- Owner/accountant/viewer roles
- Audit logging
- Admin screens
- Server-side APIs
- Hosted deployment

That explains the newer Node requirement, database migrations, Wrangler/Cloudflare components, and Linux-oriented scripts.

If this calculator only needs to accept figures, perform calculations, and export results, most of that is unnecessary. A better design would be a small browser application that runs with:

```powershell
npm install
npm run dev
```

Or it could be made completely standalone as an HTML file that opens by double-clicking—no Node, database, account, or deployment process required.

The main decision is whether you genuinely need multiple users, logins, roles, and permanent audit records. If not, I recommend simplifying it substantially.

Refactored successfully into a simple Flask application.

Run it with:

```powershell
cd D:\Dropbox\windowsdesktop\loan-statement-calculator
.\run_local.ps1
```

Then open:

```text
http://127.0.0.1:5000
```

On the first visit, create the shared username and password for you and your friend.

The replacement retains:

- Daily Actual/365 interest calculations
- Monthly loan-anniversary periods
- CSV payment imports
- Interest-first payment allocation
- Excel statement export
- Official Bank of England historical rate retrieval using its documented CSV feed ([Bank of England documentation](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/boeapps/database/Help.asp?Highlight=Hierarchy&Travel=))
- Offline rate fallback

The Node, Next.js, Cloudflare, D1 database, migrations, roles and administration system have been removed. Those deleted tracked files remain recoverable through Git.

Verification completed:

- 5 automated tests passed
- Excel export tested
- Login protection tested
- JavaScript syntax checked
- Live Bank Rate feed retrieved
- Local setup page returned HTTP 200

Instructions are in [README.md](D:\Dropbox\windowsdesktop\loan-statement-calculator\README.md). This version is deliberately local-only; the simplest way to communicate the loan currently is to export and send the Excel statement. An internet link for your friend would be the next separate deployment step.
